usage: Main page/app surface. Not for cards, popovers, or elevated layers.
Recessed or secondary surface (cards, muted areas, secondary). Not for the main page surface.
Raised surface above the default layer (popovers, dropdowns, dialogs). Not for inline card surfaces.
Inverted surface for contrast callouts. Not for general-purpose backgrounds.
Primary body and heading text. Not for secondary, placeholder, or disabled text.
Secondary or supporting text (captions, helper text, metadata). Not for primary readable content.
Emphatic text with stronger contrast when needed. Not for subtle or secondary text.
Text on top of inverse (dark) surfaces. Not for default surface text.
Text conveying a primary action (links, active button labels). Not for generic body text.
Text rendered on top of a primary action background. Not for text on neutral surfaces.
Error, danger, or destructive action text and icons, on a neutral surface or on a destructive tint. Not for general warning or informational text.
Success text and icons, on a neutral surface or on a success tint. Not for warnings, errors or neutral information.
Warning text and icons, on a neutral surface or on a warning tint. Not for errors, successes or neutral information.
Standard dividers and component outlines. Not for input fields or focus rings.
Lightweight dividers where minimal visual weight is preferred. Not for interactive element borders.
Border for form input fields. Not for decorative dividers or layout borders.
Focus ring outline for keyboard accessibility. Lighter in dark mode, so the solid part of an indicator keeps 3:1 on the dark card and on a field's fill. Not for resting or hover states.
Standard icon fill. Not for icons in branded or destructive contexts.
Muted/secondary icon fill. Not for primary interactive icons.
Icon on a primary action background. Not for icons on neutral surfaces.
Primary call-to-action button/element background. Not for secondary or ghost variants.
Text or icon on top of a primary action background. Not for text on neutral surfaces.
Error state color for backgrounds, tints and borders. Not for text, warnings or success states.
Text and icons placed on color.feedback.error.default. Never use color.text.default on an error surface.
Success state color for backgrounds, tints and borders. Not for text, warnings or errors.
Text and icons placed on color.feedback.success.default. Never use color.text.default on a success surface.
Warning state color for backgrounds and tints. Not for text, borders or icons, not for errors or successes.
Text and icons placed on color.feedback.warning.default, dark in both modes. Never use white on a warning surface.

Categorical chart Series 1 — the brand violet. For unordered categories: every series is at least 3:1 on the default and subtle surfaces of its mode, and distinguishable from the others under protanopia and deuteranopia (lint-chart-palette). Not for ordered data — use color.chart.sequential.*.

Categorical chart Series 2 — blue. For unordered categories: every series is at least 3:1 on the default and subtle surfaces of its mode, and distinguishable from the others under protanopia and deuteranopia (lint-chart-palette). Not for ordered data — use color.chart.sequential.*.

Categorical chart Series 3 — ochre, yellow in dark mode. For unordered categories: every series is at least 3:1 on the default and subtle surfaces of its mode, and distinguishable from the others under protanopia and deuteranopia (lint-chart-palette). Not for ordered data — use color.chart.sequential.*.

Categorical chart Series 4 — plum. For unordered categories: every series is at least 3:1 on the default and subtle surfaces of its mode, and distinguishable from the others under protanopia and deuteranopia (lint-chart-palette). Not for ordered data — use color.chart.sequential.*.

Categorical chart Series 5 — brown, gold in dark mode. For unordered categories: every series is at least 3:1 on the default and subtle surfaces of its mode, and distinguishable from the others under protanopia and deuteranopia (lint-chart-palette). Not for ordered data — use color.chart.sequential.*.
Sequential chart step 1 of 5, lightest to darkest. Ordered data only (a heatmap, a scale of intensity): its steps differ by lightness, not hue, so they cannot tell unordered categories apart.
Sequential chart step 2 of 5, lightest to darkest. Ordered data only (a heatmap, a scale of intensity): its steps differ by lightness, not hue, so they cannot tell unordered categories apart.

Width of the focus ring indicator (2px). Use for all focus-visible ring styles.
Horizontal padding for the main page container. Not for component-level spacing.
Vertical gap between major page sections. Not for component-level spacing.
Narrow content column max-width (42rem). Not for full-width or wide layouts.
Default content column max-width (64rem). Not for narrow or wide layouts.
Wide content column max-width (80rem). Not for narrow or default layouts.
Default sidebar width (16rem). Use for the main navigation sidebar.
Sidebar width on mobile viewports (18rem). Slightly wider for touch targets.
Sidebar width in icon-only/collapsed mode (3rem).
Extra-small text size (12px). The text of components: labels, buttons, inputs, badges, menu items, descriptions.
Small text size (14px). Use for titles inside components (CardTitle, DialogTitle) and a screen's secondary content. A field label stays text-xs.
Default body text size (16px). Use for main readable content.
Large text size (18px). Use for featured body text; Heading level 3.
XL text (20px). Heading level 2: section headings.
2XL text (24px). Heading level 1: the page title.
3XL text (30px). Hero text a screen draws; no component uses it.
4XL text (36px). Display text a screen draws, rarely; no component uses it.

Line height that `text-sm` sets with its size. `leading-*` or `text-sm/<leading>` overrides it.
Line height that `text-base` sets with its size. `leading-*` or `text-base/<leading>` overrides it.
Line height that `text-lg` sets with its size. `leading-*` or `text-lg/<leading>` overrides it.
Line height that `text-xl` sets with its size. `leading-*` or `text-xl/<leading>` overrides it.
Line height that `text-2xl` sets with its size. `leading-*` or `text-2xl/<leading>` overrides it.

Line height that `text-4xl` sets with its size. `leading-*` or `text-4xl/<leading>` overrides it.
Tight line height for short text on one or two lines. Not for paragraph text.
Snug line height: FieldLabel draws it. Not for long-form reading content.
Default line height for body text.
Relaxed line height for improved readability in long-form content.
Loose line height for highly spaced text. Not for dense UIs.
Tight letter spacing for headings: Heading draws it at every level. Not for body text.
Default letter spacing. Use as baseline.
Wide letter spacing for captions. No component draws it.
Wider letter spacing for all-caps or overline text.
Widest letter spacing, for the keyboard shortcuts of menus and the command palette.
Normal weight for body text, labels and descriptions.
Medium weight for buttons, tabs, badges and component titles. A field label stays normal.
Semibold for headings: Heading draws it at every level.
Bold for strong emphasis a screen draws, and the logo.

Secondary sans-serif typeface (Geist): Kbd keys and long-form editorial text. Loaded by next/font in lib/fonts.ts under --font-sans; this token describes that choice, it does not drive it (lint-font-tokens).

Typeface of the whole interface (JetBrains Mono), set on <html> with font-mono. Loaded by next/font in lib/fonts.ts under --font-mono; this token describes that choice, it does not drive it (lint-font-tokens).
Zero radius, square corners: the radius of every component. `rounded-none` is a static class that reads no token; only the Sonner toast reads this one.
Minimal rounding (0.4× base). The legend and tooltip indicators of a chart.
Small rounding (0.6× base). For content a screen draws itself; no component uses it.
Medium rounding (0.8× base). For content a screen draws itself; no component uses it.
Base rounding (1× = 0.625rem). For content a screen draws itself, and the shadcn --radius alias; no component reads it.
Larger rounding (1.4× base). For content a screen draws itself; no component uses it.
Extra-large rounding (1.8× base). For content a screen draws itself (a hero); no component uses it.
Very large rounding (2.2× base). Use sparingly for decorative content; no component uses it.
Maximum rounding (2.6× base). Use only for hero content; no component uses it.
Pill/full rounding. A round shape: Avatar, RadioGroup and Switch draw rounded-full, a static class that reads no token.
Minimal lift for interactive elements. Not for decorative purposes.
Small lift for cards and hover states. Not for fixed navigation.
Medium elevation for dropdowns and context menus. Not for inline content.
Large elevation for modals and side panels. Not for standard cards.
Extra-large elevation for full overlay panels. Not for inline components.
Maximum elevation for toasts and high-priority overlays. Use sparingly.
Inner shadow for pressed, inset, or sunken element states. Not for raised elements.
No duration — for immediate state changes. Not for visual transitions.
Fast micro-interactions (100ms). The default of a transition with no duration class: hover and focus feedback, and most overlays the components draw.
Standard transition duration (200ms). For a fade or a move a screen draws itself, and the Sheet's slide.
Slow, deliberate transitions (300ms). The NavigationMenu content without a viewport and its chevron, the MessageScrollerButton's exit; no modal or drawer uses it.
Slowest transitions (500ms). Use only for complex animations; no component uses it (the Drawer's own 500ms is vaul's).
Extra-slow duration (1000ms), for a transition or animate-in and animate-out. No component uses it: a keyframe loop (caret-blink, pulse, spin) sets its own duration.
Standard ease-in-out. Default for all UI transitions.
Ease-in curve. Use for elements exiting the screen.
Ease-out curve. Use for elements entering the screen.
Spring overshoot. Use for playful or bouncy interactions only.
Opacity for disabled interactive elements. Not for placeholder or overlay use.
Deprecated: placeholder text was never faded. Form fields color it with color.text.subtle.
Deprecated: modal backdrops never read it. They use a 10% static-black scrim with a backdrop blur.

The lowest global layer (1000), above the page content. No floating surface of the design system takes it: its menus, popovers and lists draw `z-popover`. Seven components raise one of their own parts with it — the AvatarBadge, a focused ButtonGroup child, a Calendar day, the active InputOTP slot, the Resizable grip, a focused ToggleGroup item and Select's scroll buttons —, a local order that specs/foundations/elevation.md gives to small raw z-index values: do not copy it.
Sticky headers/footers. Renders above dropdowns.
Fixed position elements. Renders above sticky.
Overlay/backdrop. Renders above fixed elements.
Modal dialogs. Renders above overlays.
Floating surfaces (1500): popovers, hover cards, dropdown, context and menubar menus, the Select, Combobox and NavigationMenu panels. Renders above modals, so a menu opened in a dialog shows.
Toast notifications (1600): above popovers, below tooltips. No component reads it yet: the Sonner `Toaster` keeps sonner's own z-index (999999999), above every layer of this scale.
Tooltips. Highest z-index to always appear on top.
Viewport width from which the `sm:` variant applies (mobile-first, min-width). Not a container width.
Viewport width from which the `md:` variant applies (mobile-first, min-width). Not a container width.
Viewport width from which the `lg:` variant applies (mobile-first, min-width). Not a container width.
Viewport width from which the `xl:` variant applies (mobile-first, min-width). No component needs it yet; Tailwind compiles it regardless, so the token keeps its value on record for wide layouts.
Viewport width from which the `2xl:` variant applies (mobile-first, min-width). No component needs it yet; Tailwind compiles it regardless, so the token keeps its value on record for wide layouts.

Width of every plain border: `border`, `border-t`, `divide-x`… and of the solid outline a focus indicator draws on an element without a border (`outline-(length:--border-width-default)`). Not for focus rings, which use space.focus-ring-width.
Stroke of the dashed series indicator in chart tooltips. Not for component borders.
Ring painted in the background color around an element that overlaps another, cutting it out: stacked avatars, an avatar's badge. Not for borders or focus rings.

Minimum pointer target (24px): WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), level AA. The clickable area of every control reaches it, or the control meets one of the exceptions listed in specs/foundations/size.md.
